102468.author: Hylt

102471.author: Jamey Stegmaier
102471.text: The plan has always been to release one expansion per continent. :)

102995.author: Zach Leber
102995.text: I purchased Oceania in August 2024 from B&N and just opened it today and it came with 5 double-sided folding mats with the reverse side being the original art.  That must be a recent change given Jamey’s February posts. This allows one to just keep these new mats. We loved the new birds and nectar. Thank you.

103065.author: UK Birdy Girl
103065.text: Does the game work if you  use the European Expansion cards on their own WITHOUT the original American birds?

103090.author: Jamey Stegmaier
103090.text: It does! You may run out of cards at higher player counts, but otherwise the bird cards function well in any combination with the core game and other expansions (including on their own).

103098.author: Michael Parsons
103098.text:
Ecologist bonus card : count the number of birds YOU PLAYED, in the habitat where you PLAYED the fewest birds.  .........

do you only count the habitat where you PLAYED birds ?

and not a habitat where you 'haven't'  Played any birds ?

e.g is does not say the Habitat with the fewest birds, it states YOU PLAYED the fewest birds .....  my capitals emphasis

cheers

i.e 5 in forest 4 in grassland and 0 in wetland

= 4 birds PLAYED ?

103099.author: Jamey Stegmaier
103099.text: If you have a habitat with 0 birds, you've played 0 birds into that habitat, and the Ecologist views it as 0 birds (e.g., in your example, you would score 0 points). In other words, the ecologist is looking for you to not neglect any habitat.

104610.author: Luis
104610.text:
Hi, can you share the appendix and the European Expansion files in Spanish? Thank you.

Hola! Podrían por favor compartir el apéndice del juego base y las reglas de la expansión europea en español? Gracias.

104957.author: Lesia
104957.text:
European Turtle Dove (European Expansion): "Draw 1 new bonus card. Then gain 1 food from the birdfeeder, lay 1 egg on any bird, or draw 1." (When Played).

Does this mean:

 - if you get new bonus card, then you can choose 1 food OR 1 egg OR 1 card;

 - if you get new bonus card, then you can choose 1 food AND 1 egg OR 1 card.

After taking the bonus, can you take only one of the three resources anyway? Can you take both food and an egg?

I will be very grateful for your answer.

104976.author: Jamey Stegmaier
104976.text:
First, draw 1 bonus card.

Second, choose one of the following three benefits to gain:

-1 food from the birdfeeder

-lay 1 egg on any bird

-draw 1 bird card

Then you're done! :)

105056.author: Alex
105056.text: Wit the birds where you can move them to another habitat if they’re on the far right, if you have 2 in the last and 2nd last, can you move both in the same turn?

105058.author: Jamey Stegmaier
105058.text: You activate each ability one at a time, so you could activate the first (move it), then activate the second (move it). You're only moving the bird, not moving your action token-it remains in the same habitat where you started the turn.

105607.author: Arlene ward
105607.text: What does the power card mean. When a vulturre bird is a success?

105615.author: Jamey Stegmaier
105615.text: That icon is referring to predatory birds. These birds have powers like, "Reveal the top card of the deck. If it's smaller than 50cm, tuck it under this card." A "success" means that they revealed a card they can actually tuck.

105939.author: Mark Dutton
105939.text: Can you receive multiple food tokens of any type equal to the number of matching dice in the feeder, counting as only 1 food action?  Example: 3 dice in feeder, 2 fish, 1 wheat.  You are to collect two food.  You take 2 fish as your first food action since they match, then reroll dice in feeder, showing 2 more fish, 1 invertebrate, 1 wheat and 1 mouse.  You take 2 fish again, since they match as your second food action.  I've seen some videos on Wingspan where either the automa or players take food in this fashion.  Is this permitted?

105942.author: Jamey Stegmaier
105942.text:
Thanks for your question! This is not a thing. :) Whenever you see the icon of a food die, that means to gain 1 food token matching a dice result, then remove that die from the birdfeeder.

What you're probably seeing in videos is instances where there are 2 such icons-this appears on the player mat in some places. Since there are 2 icons, you gain 2 food. But if you only see 1 icon, you only gain 1 food.

If you know of a video that contradicts this, please reply with the video link and the timestamp of when the mistake is made. I'm happy to take a look to clarify what's happening.

106072.author: Mark Dutton
106072.text: Thank you for the quick response.  Here is a video of automa play, where the automa takes multiple foods of the same type from the feeder.  Go to 21:50 of video.  Is this accurate for how the automa would remove dice from the feeder when taking food?  This is what had me thinking a player would be able to do the same thing when taking food if the dice happened to match.

106076.author: Jamey Stegmaier
106076.text: This is an Automa-specific rule; as a human player, you can't do things the same way the Automa does.

106393.author: Ever woodward
106393.text: When a card says roll all dice not in the bird feeder, if any are mice, (fish, etc) cache on this card, what if  there is already a target food in the feeder but the dice rolled are not that food. Do you chache the food token? Or only if one of the recently rolled dice are that food? Thanks!

106407.author: Jamey Stegmaier
106407.text: For those abilities, you only look at the dice you roll (which are rolled outside of the birdfeeder).

107177.author: Sal (plantlassie)
107177.text:
Hello! I have two questions. 

1) Does Stonemaier Games have a Discord server? I poked around and found a Wingspan Digital Discord server, but I’m more interested in work that the original company that designed the game rather than the one that adapted it for digital play. (Although I have respect and appreciation for Monster Couch)

If the answer to #1 is no, is there a formal avenue I can take to reach out to someone representing the company about creating a Discord server for them?

#2. I see that three more expansions are in Wingspan’s future, that is very exciting, and gives me pause to ponder a couple of questions.

2a. Will there be an edition once all the expansions are out that includes all six expansions for the game for a single purchase? It seems bulky to have six different boxes, even if an expansion changes the mechanics slightly.

2b. Is there any estimation for a timeline of when we can expect each or any of the expansions?

2c. Once Wingspan has published all six expansions for the game, will Stonemaier be working on other games? Forgive my ignorance regarding the company’s current projects beyond Wingspan. This may be mentioned on the website.

2d. Is there any chance that we could expect similar versions of Wingspan that feature other animals? Maybe either Collector’s Editions for holidays (ex. bat spin-off for Halloween—there are ~1,400 species of bats) or the like? Not sure if Wyrmspan is also designed by Stonemaier, but that comes to mind when exploring this topic. 

Thank you so much for your time to answer all these silly questions!

107178.author: Jamey Stegmaier
107178.text:
1. We do! It's listed near the footer of our various newsletters: https://stonemaiergames.com/discord/

2a. No, the only way we'll sell Wingspan content is the current method (each expansion is a separate purchase and the core game is also separate so people can pick and choose exactly what they want, whenever they want). You won't need 6 boxes; probably more like 2 or 3, or just 1 if you get the Nesting Box.

2b. Whenever Elizabeth is ready, which is probably once every 2-3 years. You can see project statuses on our News page and in the World of Wingspan newsletter.

2c. Yes, we have many other games (see the All Games menu), including Wyrmspan, which has some similar mechanisms to Wingspan.

2d. Wyrmspan is indeed published by Stonemaier Games, and it's possible we'll have one more game in the future that features animals and shares some mechanisms with Wingspan (I can't answer spoiler questions, so that's the most I can say about the future).

Given your curiosity, I highly recommend looking through the World of Wingspan newsletters (they're archived here: https://stonemaiergames.com/games/wingspan/) and subscribing to it! :)

107559.author: Sal (plantlassie)
107559.text: Thank you for taking the time to reply. <3

107751.author: Søren
107751.text:
Hi Nadia

I wrote Asmodee Nordics. And positive news there are working on a danish translation but it is still so early that they do not know the release date. They hope for 2025 release

107850.author: Pierre-Olivier
107850.text: Hi! Could you add the rules in french on the dropbox? Have a great holiday season! :)

107852.author: Jamey Stegmaier
107852.text: Thanks for asking! The French rules aren't ours to share, but feel free to ask Matagot, our French partner. :)

108336.author: Matthew Sherwood
108336.text:
Duet Mode two questions...

1. What should happen to duet token when you have a bird that when activates, it would move to another habitat?

2. DUET mode

If I have a duet in the reset zone, can I say reset the bird feeder partway through taking food.  So there are 4 food items available,  I take one, then can i now reset the feeder in hopes of getting something not already available.

108361.author: Jamey Stegmaier
108361.text:
Thanks for these questions! 

1. You only place a duet token when you play a bird, so nothing would happen with duet tokens when you move a bird.

2.  That's right!

108450.author: Yin
108450.text:
Hi,

I am pretty sure this question has not been asked yet, hopefully.

If I have Red-Tailed Hawk (.. if less than 75cm, tuck it behind this card..) on first spot in Wetland. And,

Ruddy Duck (Draw 2 cards. If you do discard 1 card…) on the second spot of Wetland. 

I want to play draw cards action, ie the 3rd spot of Wetland. I will pick two cards, from the face up deck. Then activate Ruddy Duck, pick the last one from face up deck and draw the second from the (face down) deck.

When I want to activate power of Red-Tailed Hawk, does it mean I am not able to activate? Given there is no card on face up deck? 

Thanks for responding in advance. We like this games so much.

108451.author: Jamey Stegmaier
108451.text: Thanks Yin! Whenever you draw cards, unless the card specifies otherwise, you can draw them from the 3 face-up cards on the bird tray or from the top of the deck. The Red-Tailed Hawk specifically mentions that you're looking at the top card of the deck (not the 3 face-up cards)-there will always be cards in the deck.

108453.author: Yin
108453.text:
Thank you. We have been playing it wrong. This now make more sense. 

Thank you for clarifying

108674.author: Sally
108674.text: Sacred Kingfisher: pink power, but marked as a predator power. Does this mean another player's bird with 'predator succeeds' can collect each time the pink power is used? Seems wrong to me, but we don't agree.

108675.author: Joe Aubrey
108675.text: Yes! If the Sacred Kingfisher gains a food with its power, then it is definitely a predator "succeeding."

109104.author: Trevor Hurlow
109104.text: Spangled Drongo  card (Oceana) - during a round "when another player gains a Nectar this card gains a nectar from the supply" does this mean that during a round a player gains a nectar for any reason - not just gaining food  - they Spangled drongo enables the owner to draw a nectar

109108.author: Jamey Stegmaier
109108.text: Thanks Trevor! This is a "once between turns" power, so while it does mean what you described, it can only trigger once between each of your turns, not every time.

109153.author: Nick Magic
109153.text:
but, Jamey, wait. Appendix says differently:

"These are push-your-luck powers: After each roll, you

check to see whether you succeeded or failed. Once

you fail, this bird’s activation is over. You also may

choose to end the bird’s activation at any time to avoid

the risk of failing and losing what you have gained.

If you failed, you must stop and return all food cached

by this bird during the current activation of this power.

If you succeeded, cache 1 food on this bird from the

supply (do not cache more than one food after each

roll). Then, if you have rolled fewer than 3 times during

the current activation of this power, decide whether to

roll again."

This tells me that the sequence will go something like this:

Player A: Activates Purple Heron

Player A: Rolls 2 dice, caches a grub on the Heron (I would count this as a success after a roll)

Player B: Activates the pink power, as he/she notices that the Food is cached successfully during an opponents turn (it doesn't have to wait 'till the end of Player A's turn) (core of the pink power rules)

Player A: Decides if he/she is going to risk his/her own reward by rolling again. Future rolls should have nothing to do with Player B's Turkey Vulture (neither, a success nor a failure)

Right?

109154.author: Jamey Stegmaier
109154.text: Nick: I don't think the appendix contradicts my answer, but it certainly is open to interpretation. I'm interpreting success/failure as whether or not you end up with anything as the result of hunt power. It doesn't seem like a successful hunt action if you don't end up with a benefit from it, right? But I can also see your point in relation to what other players want-your interpretation is friendlier to the player with the Turkey Vulture. I'll check with someone else on my team to see what they think.

109168.author: Nat A
109168.text: Hello! My brother and I played the Oceania expansion for the first time this Christmas, and I had a question about the Brown Falcon. The text says "Look at a card from the deck. If its food cost includes an invertebrate or a rodent, tuck it behind this bird. If not, discard it." I drew a card with a wild food symbol, and we could not decide if that card should be tucked or not? I still won, but clarification would be appreciated. :)

109169.author: Jamey Stegmaier
109169.text: A wild wouldn’t count for a card that’s looking for a specific icon. Thanks for playing!

109697.author: Oliver
109697.text: Any chance of getting a turn timer for offline mode of the digital games?

109710.author: Jamey Stegmaier
109710.text: This is a digital timer, right? If so, please send the request to support@monstercouch.com or the Wingspan Discord server, where they have a bug reporting channel (https://discord.gg/wingspan).

110510.author: Julian
110510.text: Just curious if any of the proceeds and profits from Wingspan have been directed to wildlife and ecological conservation efforts to birds? With Finspan coming out as well, it seems appropriate that birds and fish could receive some benefit and ecological support as they make the game so popular. If it listed throughout the website, I may not have seen it. Lovely game, cant wait for Finspan as well :)

110521.author: Jamey Stegmaier
110521.text:
Julian: If you look at the pages for the Wingspan expansions, you'll see information about these donations:

"Due to the sheer number of birds affected by the Australian wildfires, Stonemaier Games announced early that the next expansion for Wingspan will focus on the region of Oceania. For each email we collected by January 22, Stonemaier Games donated $1 to WIRES, a wildlife rescue organization in Australia. Our total donation was $7,439 USD ($10,834 AUD)."

"For every preorder launch notification request we received for Wingspan Asia, Stonemaier Games donated $1 to charitable organizations that benefit birds in Asia. We split the donation total of $13,130 equally among BirdLife International, Animals Asia, Flight, and the International Crane Foundation."

There's also our annual charity auction ($188,852 to 115 charities, half of which is a money match from us: https://boardgamegeek.com/geeklist/345133/stonemaier-games-2024-charity-auction), plus the $10,000 we donated for Finspan a few days ago.

110706.author: George Ford
110706.text: If your opponent plays the Greater Adjutant or the Indian Vulture and they would stand to score more points from your bonus card than you, can you opt to not score that bonus card?

110707.author: Jamey Stegmaier
110707.text: No, you score all bonus cards you have at the end of the game (even if you earn 0 VP from them).

110916.author: Mark Dutton
110916.text: When tallying nectar at the end of the game while playing automa, do you use the sum of the nectar in all three habitats or do you use the 5/2 scoring rule for each habitat and use the sum of the 5/2 scoring?  Thank you.  Loving the game!

110918.author: David Studley
110918.text: Hi Mark. You use the amount of nectar that Automa has in each habitat to compete for majority, giving you and her 5 or 2 points for each habitat based upon who had more. Have fun!

111399.author: Vera
111399.text: Do you start with new cards in round 2, or do you continue where you left off when round 1 ended?

111400.author: Jamey Stegmaier
111400.text: You continue where you left off. The only thing that changes as the end of the round is the shared card display-remove those 3 face-up cards and replace them with 3 cards from the deck.

112243.text:

How do I get replacement items?

112245.author: Jamey Stegmaier
112245.text:
Thanks for playing Wingspan so much! We sell extra scorepads here: https://store.stonemaiergames.com/products/extra-scorepad-for-wingspan?_pos=1&_psq=scorepad&_ss=e&_v=1.0

For missing tokens, please fill out this form: https://stonemaiergames.com/about/replacement-parts/

112364.author: Simon
112364.text:
Hi!

I would like the swedish version of Wingspan European Expansion, but it seems to be out of stock everywhere. When will it be in store again?

Best regards

112365.author: Jamey Stegmaier
112365.text: We only make English-language games, so please ask Asmodee Nordics.

112377.author: Ashley
112377.text:
Hello,

I recently purchased the Asia and Oceania expansions. I am a little confused by the double sided boards in Wingspan Asia. I take it that you can use one side of the Wingspan Asia board to enter Flock mode and make the base game a 6-7 player game. But what about the other side? With the Oceania expansion it says it is capped at a 5 player game, and comes with 5 player boards. What do you use the 2 extra boards in Wingspan Asia for? An Oceania Flock mode? Any help is appreciated. Thanks.

112378.author: Jamey Stegmaier
112378.text:
Thanks Ashley! Wingspan Asia comes with 2 player mats for two reasons: One, for Flock mode, as you mentioned. Two, Wingspan Asia can be played 1-2 players by itself (i.e., someone can buy it and play with it even if they don't own the Wingspan core game).

For you, if you already have the original Wingspan game, the 2 new player mats are just for Flock mode (or for use in any 1-5 player game if you prefer the art on them).

112380.author: Ashley
112380.text: So Oceania can be played in Flock mode too? That's great. I'll have to give that a try :) Thanks!

112382.author: Jamey Stegmaier
112382.text: That's right! As noted on page 3 of the Wingspan Asia rulebook (flock mode setup), "If playing [flock mode] with the Oceania Expansion, each group uses 2 nectar dice and 3 regular food dice."

112463.author: Hunt
112463.text: Can you play flock mode with just Asia and Oceania, without the core game? Thanks

112478.author: Jamey Stegmaier
112478.text: Almost! Though you would be short 4-5 sets of player tokens and you would be missing a bunch of goal tiles and bonus cards.

112570.author: Kaven Gray
112570.text: If I play the Great Indian Bustard mid game (eg during round 2) can I score the Winter Feeder or the Visionary Leader bonus card even though they specifically state “at end of game”?

112601.author: ippei
112601.text:
My family and I enjoy playing the game.

I'd like you to sell "Wingspan Fan Art Pack" in Japan.

Are there  "Fan Art Pack" to sell  in Japan?

112618.author: Jamey Stegmaier
112618.text: Thank you! We do have the fan art pack for shipping to Japan (in English): https://aus.stonemaiergames.com/products/wingspan-fan-art-cards?_pos=1&_psq=fan+art&_ss=e&_v=1.0

114799.author: Taylor
114799.text:
Regarding Solo Asia+Oceania. I didn’t see anywhere in the Asia Solo rulebook that states Oceania is compatible with the Duet mode solo. I’m assuming it is. I’ve read the Oceania solo rulebook and automa starts with 3/4/5 nectar on each habitat, depending on difficulty. Just seems cumbersome to have two rulebooks to go back and forth between to make sure I’m playing correctly. 

The rulebook did a good at expanding the expansions for the multiplayer version, but not so much the solo version. 

It would be nice/convenient to have a comprehensive rulebook combing all the expansions for solo play. As for now, I’m just hoping I’m playing it correctly. Thank you for reading.

114807.author: David Studley
114807.text:
Hi Taylor. Thanks for sharing your thoughts on this. The Wingspan Asia Automa is compatible with all of the Wingspan expansions to date. The Asia Automa rulebook is comprehensive in that it supports both Asia and the original game rules. While the Automa Asia rules support all of the expansion, it does not include all of the rules for the expansions.  The Oceania expansion, with its addition of nectar in particular, would have added a few pages for it to be truly comprehensive.  I hope you are enjoying regardless.  Please let me know if you have any questions regarding the combination of the Automa Oceania and Asia rulesets and I'll be happy to help.

Cheers, David

115124.author: Don Strong
115124.text: End of round goals - Birds with tucked cards - Does predators with tucked cards count as well?

115375.author: Juan Blazquez
115375.text:
Hello. I have two questions:

First. I was playing solo mode and the last round goal was "number of birds on the wetland". I had 5 birds in my wetland, but it happened that automa ended up with the 3 starting birds for the last round goal plus 3 cubes, total 6 birds. Did we tie considering I maximized my available space or did automa win anyways?

Second. Does the many-colored fruit dove count for the photographer bonus card?

Thx

115436.author: David Studley
115436.text:
Hi Juan. The Automa cannot exceed 5 birds for the “birds in

a specific habitat row” goal. So, you tied for the goal. 

Regarding the many-colored fruit dove, despite its many colors, it's not a specific color and does not count for the photographer bonus card.

Have fun,

David

116208.author: George Ford
116208.text: If I use a yellow power that lets me play a bird at game end and play the Spoon-billed Sandpiper whose power  says “When played: Draw 2 new bonus cards and keep 1. Other players may discard any 2 resources to do the same.” Do the other players get to use that power even though it is at game end and not during the game? Thank you for clarification!

116224.author: Jamey Stegmaier
116224.text: Yes, you just follow the instructions on the power, including the portion involving other players. Thanks for playing!

116933.author: Francine Nearing
116933.text: Teal card: "This bird counts double toward the end of round goal, if it qualifies for the goal"  So, if the end of round goal is "Eggs in cavity nest", this bird would qualify by having eggs on the teal card.  Do we double the total count of eggs in cavity nests, or only the eggs on the teal card?  Another example: Goal is "birds in a row".  This round end power would qualify ONLY if it is in the row, correct?  And THEN, what is doubled....the total # of cards in the row OR just count the teal card as two cards adding 1 point to the total?

116934.author: Jamey Stegmaier
116934.text:
Thanks for playing, Francine! There are three cards like this; I think you're referring to the Eurasian Green Woodpecker, yes? If you have 2 eggs on the Woodpecker, they would count as 4 eggs for a related round-end goal.

For a goal related to birds in a specific habitat, the Woodpecker would only count if it's in that habitat (it would count as 2 birds instead of 1).

117093.author: MJE
117093.text: Duet Mode Matching Question - when matching a Duet token for a card where the food requirement is “wild,” can the Duet token go on any food space on the Duet map or only the specific one that you play?  Same for birds with / - can the token only go on the specific food that you use?

117122.author: Jamey Stegmaier
117122.text: Here's the note from the rulebook about this (page 10): "Note that it is not enough for a bird to have the correct habitat or food on the card; you must have played the bird in that habitat and used that food when playing the bird."

117332.author: Francine Nearing
117332.text: The ROUND END CARD "this bird counts double toward the end of the round goal....if it qualifies"  Let's say the goal tile is for "eggs in Wetland".  This bird is in the Wetland habitat and has 3 eggs.  I also have 5 other eggs in the habitat.  How does the round end card score?  6 eggs?  16 eggs?

117334.author: Jamey Stegmaier
117334.text: For the purpose of this goal, the bird counts as having 6 eggs instead of 3.

117348.author: Forrest
117348.text:
I have a question about the teal power of the Common Goldeneye. It states that I can place 1 egg on this bird for each other cavity nest bird I have. Does this include bird cards with the star as a nest type?

(In our house we call these birds "Star-belly sneetches.")

117352.author: Jamey Stegmaier
117352.text: Thanks, Forrest! It does include wild-habitat birds (stars). :)

117354.text:
Definition of "birds that allow you to score"

Example ENDANGERED SPECIES, PROTECTOR CARD.

117385.author: Jamey Stegmaier
117385.text: Can you provide the full text of those cards? Thanks!

117774.text: Jamey, the teal “doubling” birds only double for goals looking for birds, not eggs

117963.author: Brent F.
117963.text:
Rules question I can't find answer to. We assume the answer is no but here it goes.

Active player activated "Common Myna" which says "When activated: copy the "when activated" (brown) power of a bird in the Prarie of the player on your left"

Player to the left only has "Blue Grosbeak" which reads "when activated: if this bird is to the right of all lithe birds in is habitat, move it to another habitat."

So the question is: since common myna can only be in the prairie, can it change habitats?

117991.author: Joe Aubrey
117991.text: For the purposes of this niche situation, you can think of the Common Myna as only being able to be "played" in the prairie. It's not limited to where else it might fly! So if the Common Myna copies the Blue Grosbeak (and the Myna is to the right of all other birds in its habitat), it can move to another habitat.

119103.author: SH
119103.text: That was just the info I was looking for, I look forward to the Danish version being released.

119144.author: Michael B
119144.text: Just purchased Oceania and the player boards in the box are double sided. Everything I see online says the Oceania player boards should be one sided while the Asia boards are double sided. Was there a change made at some point or did I get the wrong components?

119145.author: Jamey Stegmaier
119145.text: The Oceania player mats are printed on both sides (one side with the faux leather and the other with the habitats). It would be strange if you received the mats with habitats printed on both sides, though not entirely out of the ordinary-as long as one of the sides of the mats has the Oceania habitats and graphic design, you're all set!

119172.author: Yin
119172.text:
My son and me fight over this.

With “Food Web Expert” bonus card, does bird card with food cost worm or cherry counted for 2 points?

119182.author: Jamey Stegmaier
119182.text: Food Web Expert looks at birds that eat only worms, so if there's any other icon on the bird, it counts for 0 points. Here's what the appendix says: ""Count the number of birds that have (invertebrate symbol) in their food cost and no other symbols."

119200.author: Michael B
119200.text: Thanks for the reply. I actually bought a second copy from a totally different retailer, and it included the double sided boards as well (not the “leather”). So it seems like the details of what comes in the box might need to be updated. Thanks

119201.author: Jamey Stegmaier
119201.text: For Oceania? That's really interesting. When I saw your question, I looked at the digital file, and it's single-sided. Perhaps it isn't up to date. I have a recollection of switching them to double-sided at some point so people didn't need to keep both the original and the Oceania mats, though.

119208.author: Michael B
119208.text: Correct, Oceania. Reading though other comments on here seem to also indicate a change at some point.

120330.author: Nick
120330.text:
Greetings, Jamey! Big fan of yours asking.

I am late to the Wingspan party, purchased all of the expansions in my country (your official partner in Ukraine - Ігромаг), except Oceania. They said they are out of print and new batch is not expected to come, since they depend on your print to localize. Can you please elaborate of what to expect - will there be another one, or just go for english version?

120338.author: Jamey Stegmaier
120338.text: Nick: I can't speak for our localization partners, but I think it's highly likely that we will reprint Oceania in English in the future.

120342.author: Nick
120342.text:
Thanks for quick reply! What I was curious is if they are really dependant on you printing it? For some reason I thought that they can reprint it regardless of english version print.

Here is their official response to me: We are not expecting a new edition of the expansion at the moment, as our boxes are printed together with the worldwide edition, so a lot depends on the game publisher.

p.s. sorry to bother you with this, but our play-group is literally dying to finally get sweet nectar :))

120367.author: Wingspanlover
120367.text: I have a question regarding honey buzzard(kernebider), when resetting birdfeeder/house, does spineless/corn count towards (all corn) or is it only the dice with corn symbols?

120369.author: Joe Aubrey
120369.text:
The European Honey Buzzard says this: "ROUND END: Reset the birdfeeder. If you do, gain all invertebrate in the birdfeeder after resetting."

So yes, you can take all invertebrates (spineless, in your words) that are showing. This includes the dice showing invertebrate/seed.

120370.author: Wingspanlover
120370.text: Thank you for your reply, I an terribly sorry, but I meant the Hawfinch powers

120371.author: Joe Aubrey
120371.text:
The Hawfinch says this: "WHEN ACTIVATED: Reset the birdfeeder. If you do, gain 1 seed from the birdfeeder after resetting."

Yes, you can take a seed (corn, in your words) from a die face showing invertebrate/seed.

120374.author: Wingspanlover
120374.text: Thank you for the clarification, I just discovered a different in the translation on the card compared to the rulebook, the Hawfinch car clearly states “all seeds” while the rulebook says 1 seed, what can I do about this? I can see how this can cause confusion playing with others?

120393.author: Joe Aubrey
120393.text: Good to know! I don't think you mentioned which language your game is in, but this is something you should report to that language's publisher (listed on the box). The difference won't cause any confusion at your table. Go ahead and play your Hawfinch card as it's written.

121008.author: Steve
121008.text: Rodney, AWESOME video (as usual).  My family plans to play this expansion tomorrow and we are looking forward to it.  AND, love your sense of humor - agree that actual chocolate eggs wouldn’t last too long! ;)

121201.author: David Natzke
121201.text: Question:  a brown power that says,  if you lay and egg on this bird during your turn tuck a card from the supply.  If I’m in a different habitat during my turn and put and egg on that card do I then get to tuck a card or only when I’m in that specific habitat can I do this action?

121202.author: Jamey Stegmaier
121202.text: It's only when you activate that power, so only when you're using that specific habitat.

121205.author: Jeri Krebs
121205.text: Hello! Thank you for creating such an innovative and aesthetically pleasing game. I have enjoyed it so much that my birdfeeder is falling apart. The card board is pulling apart in layers on the corners. Is there a way to replace it or restore it? I would even be interested in paying for one that is more durable.

121206.author: Jamey Stegmaier
121206.text: Thanks for playing Wingspan so much! There are a number of third-party creators who make wooden birdfeeders (search for Tower Rex, for example). If you don't like those options, you can fill out our replacement parts form and we'll send you another birdfeeder punchboard.

121629.author: Andreas
121629.text: I thoroughly enjoy playing Wingspan with my kids. Since they are not fluent in English, we have had good use for the Swedish localisations of the European and Oceania expansions. Will there ever be a Swedish translation of the Asia expansion as well?

121668.author: Jamey Stegmaier
121668.text: Thanks Andreas-I hope so! That's up to Asmodee Nordics. Feel free to let them know you want this expansion in Swedish.

123416.author: Hunt
123416.text: Does the common myna copy a brown power from another player because mynas are known for copying (parroting) sounds like talking? Just wondering if you guys had thought of that.

123417.author: Jamey Stegmaier
123417.text: Yes, birds in Wingspan are designed theme-first. You can see that the fun fact on the Common Myna card is about how they are skilled mimics, hence the design of their gameplay power. :)

123560.author: Jina Hill
123560.text: Hi there, we are very new to the game. For the "when activated" birds, do they get "activated" only one time in the game or do they activate each time an action  (lay eggs, draw a card) is used in that row? We were playing that a bird could only be activated once, but we don't see a way to track if it has happened or not.  If they can be activated multiple times, can you activate only one power each action or can you do all of the birds each time that action is done (lay ing eggs, drawing a bird, etc.). The rules surroudnkig this are not clear to us. Thank you.

123563.author: Jamey Stegmaier
123563.text: Jina: Thanks for trying Wingspan! On your turn, if you choose to activate a habitat (i.e., the wetlands, where you draw cards), you may activate every "when activated" card in that habitat from right to left. This is detailed on page 4 of the rules and elsewhere. I highly recommend watching the Watch It Played rules video for Wingspan, as it goes over the rules in a different way that I find helpful.

123688.author: Scott
123688.text: Follow up auto this, if on the first reset there is one food I want, so I take it, can I now pay the 1 food cost to reset again and take a second food?

123689.author: Jamey Stegmaier
123689.text: In general, yes, you can reset the birdfeeder (if applicable) after choosing 1 food.

123697.author: Scott
123697.text: Hi Jerry, thank you for responding. We just tried the scenario on the online version and once we drew a food cube, it removed the option to pay a food to reset the feeder. Just an fyi. Love the game!!!

123698.author: Scott
123698.text: Jamey! Sorry for the miss on your name! I guess I was just excited!😀

123701.author: Jamey Stegmaier
123701.text: Thanks Scott! Feel free to report the bug to Monster Couch-that should help.

124166.author: Joël
124166.text:
Can you add Wingspan Asia to Wingspan base +EE+OC?

So how do you play this game with everything released? Just adding the bird/bonuscards and the duetboard to everything else? Does this play good or is it beter to play with less? Kind regards!

124167.author: Jamey Stegmaier
124167.text: You can! You can play Wingspan in any combination (mixing bonus cards and bird cards; it's only the goal tiles that are different in the Duet mode).

124181.author: Hunt
124181.text: Another question about "copying" powers: Can the Rose-Ringed Parakeet (when played: copy a white power off another player's board) copy the Eastern Imperial Eagle/Bonelli's Eagle power (for each rat in this bird's cost, you may pay one bird card from your hand, then tuck them behind this bird)? The parakeet doesn't eat rats. Am I looking at the food cost of the bird I am copying or the parakeet itself? Believe it or not, this question has come up in a game before...

124185.author: Joe Aubrey
124185.text: The power says "copy a white power." It doesn't say to copy anything else, like food requirements. Imagine that power written on the Rose-Ringed Parakeet. So if you chose to copy this bird's power, you wouldn't be able to pay the bird's cost by tucking from your hand because it does not have rodent food costs. So that'd probably be a poor choice of white power to copy. ;)

124540.author: Amar
124540.text: When a bird power tells me to take food from the bird feeder and that I “may” cache it on this card, does that mean I don’t have to if I don’t want to?

124541.author: Jamey Stegmaier
124541.text: If it specifically says "may," you may gain the food to your supply or to cache on the bird-your choice.

124542.author: Amar
124542.text: Thanks Jamey, I've been having a tough time convincing everyone (particularly a guy name Shan) what the word "may" meant as other cards with similar abilities exclude the word "may". This provides much needed light. Thanks!

124563.author: Leroy
124563.text: If we are at last round of game with only 1 egg left, and person triggers lay eggs during their turn, are they able to grab the egg before other with brown abilities grab it?

124928.author: Martha
124928.text:
Actually, you CAN spend food (wheat) cached on the Eurasian Nuthatch and the Coal Tit (from the European expansion). “At any time, you may spend [wheat] cached on this card.” 

On a related note: Does the spendable food cached on the Eurasian Nuthatch and the Coal Tit count as “Food remaining in your supply at game end” for the Winter Feeder bonus?

124929.author: Jamey Stegmaier
124929.text: There is no limit to eggs—just use another token to represent it.

124932.author: Jamey Stegmaier
124932.text: You're absolutely right about those specific birds! Cached food isn't in your supply (even for special birds like that), though.

125532.author: Lindsey
125532.text: Re-roll question: If there is 1 rat and 2 wheat in the feeder, and someone’s turn is to pick 2 foods from the feeder, can they take the rat and then re-roll the dice to choose their second food since the remaining 2 were both wheat? Or, since there were 2 available options at the start of their turn, do they have to choose from the rat and 2 wheats with no re-roll?

125545.author: Jamey Stegmaier
125545.text: Thank for your question! Food dice are selected one at a time, so the player could pick the rat, rest the bird feeder, then choose their second food.

125574.author: Paul Lewis
125574.text: For the push-your-luck birds in Asia, wording allows for dice to be selected from inside and outside the feeder.   Are they returned to original location after completing the brown power (with original side up for those in the feeder) or do they all get paced outside the feeder?

125579.author: Michelle Styles
125579.text: Question about the Eurasian Green Woodpecker. If this bird has been played on a player mat and the end of round goal is cards in hand, does this bird double the cards in hand? I don’t think it “qualifies”for the round end goal but my opponent disagreed. Thank you!

125580.author: Michelle Styles
125580.text: Is there a way to search the comments?  If so, can you tell me how? As an example, I would like to be able to search for other questions regarding specific birds so that I can easily see if my question has already been asked. Thank you!

125593.author: Jamey Stegmaier
125593.text: You can! Great question. Either here or on the FAQ page, scroll down and click “see all comments”. The hit control-f and type the name of the bird. Googling it can also help, as it will bring up results on BoardGameGeek.

125594.author: Jamey Stegmaier
125594.text: Thanks for checking! Since they’re rolled outside the birdfeeder, that’s where they remain.

125607.author: Joe Aubrey
125607.text: You are right! The Eurasian Green Woodpecker does not qualify for the end of round goal counting cards in hand. (And if you had kept it in your hand, it still would not count double because the power isn't in effect until after you play it.) Birds like these are helpful for other end of round goals.

125661.author: John Ritchie
125661.text:
Hello, loving the game, thank you! I have a couple of questions:

1: American Oystercatcher. When Played draw bird cards equal to the number of players +1... each player chooses 1 of those cards. Q - can we look at the cards before choosing, or are they chosen 'blind'?

2: Am I right in thinking that if a card says 'Draw a bird card from the deck', because it's specific it must come from the deck; but if a card just says 'Draw a bird card' then that can be either from the deck or one of the three face-up cards?

125665.author: Jamey Stegmaier
125665.text:
Thanks for these questions!

1. Players look at the cards and choose (it isn’t blind). 

2. You are exactly correct.

126052.author: Steve Spisak
126052.text: Australia Ibis question:  If the last player to play in a round, and takes cards from the display, is the display refilled (which would only get immediate discarded), which makes them available to only the Ibis player.

126108.author: Steve Spisak
126108.text: Another way to ask the same question:  are the cards refilled, even if it the end of the entire round?

126109.author: Jamey Stegmaier
126109.text: The display is refilled at the end of a player's turn, so yes, it would be refilled at the end of the Australian Ibis player's turn. Then all players would proceed with the round end steps, which includes completely refreshing the card row.

126770.author: Rebekah
126770.text: We voted on the type of box for the next Wingspan expansion. I'm curious what the price difference would be between the folding box and standard two piece box. We use our two piece boxes, but if it cuts the price in half or something, we'd rather do the folding box.

126771.author: Jamey Stegmaier
126771.text: The exact price difference depends on the quantities produced, but somewhere between $5-10 (this is the customer price, not the cost to make the boxes).

126795.author: Matt
126795.text: Hi Jamey, in response to the world of wingspan survey you just put out, there was no section for comments so I thought I'd leave one here. I've selected 2 piece box for the upcoming expansion because I'm at capacity with all other wingspan content. I don't own the nesting box (and not interested in owning it) so a recyclable box means I'm going to have to look at alternative storage solutions which defeats the purpose of a recyclable box. I understand the want to recycle and keep the price down. It's going to be hard to find a solution to fit everybody. There's no way of doing both? Or doing the two piece box as standard. And offer the content just in a plain brown cardboard box on the webstore, like the apiary expansion, and the vision improved cards, for people who really don't want another box. Thanks for always asking by the way. Cheers, Matt.

126797.author: Jamey Stegmaier
126797.text: The folding box provides the same capacity as a 2-piece box-why couldn't you use it for storage just like a 2-piece box? Both boxes are recyclable, and the utility of both boxes is the same. The only difference is price.

126821.author: Anthony
126821.text: Hi there, big wingspan fan here. Thankyou for bringing this game into my life, I had to get the nesting box to keep it all in. I was wondering if it might be possible in the next expansion for wingspan for a buildable cardboard deck holder. When we play we mostly work through the stack (multiple expansions) over 3-5 games. It would be nice to have a thematic (much lile the bird trays) solution to hold the deck vertical on the table. Thankyou again

126843.author: JRT
126843.text: It would be nice if the Fan Art packs and upcoming Fan Card Packs came with a separator for the Nesting Box.  Yes, the Nesting Box did come with blanks that we can use.

126844.author: Jamey Stegmaier
126844.text: In case it helps, we designed the fan art box to fit into the bottom layer of the Nesting Box. There's already a "promo" separator in the Nesting Box to use for the fan card packs.

126846.author: JRT
126846.text:
Box questionnaire additional comment:

Our extended family owns 4 copies, with all expansions, 3 with Nesting Box.  

Ironically, we got rid of the 2-part boxes, but kept the Fan-Art pack box because unlike other categories, they are an alternative set of the same cards.

126847.author: JRT
126847.text:
Gee Jamey, 2 minutes to reply, can't you do it faster? !

Great point.  That's exactly where we store the Fan Art box (with cards), rather than the main slots above.

126934.author: Ilsa Govan
126934.text: I'm not sure where to share this, but I noticed a glitch in the new online Asia expansion. I played the savannah sparrow, which allows me to play another bird in the meadow. However, it allowed me to play the rose-ringed parakeet in the forest.

126935.author: Jamey Stegmaier
126935.text: Thank you! Please report bugs to support@monstercouch.com or the Wingspan Discord server, where they have a bug reporting channel (https://discord.gg/wingspan).

126998.author: Dick
126998.text:
Playing the MonsterCouch computer version of Wingspan I just used the Gray Wagtail to gain two Nectar and then immediately after the round end takes them away again.

I am assuming this is as intended and your answer was factually correct but it's not a smart strategy. :)

127003.author: Jamey Stegmaier
127003.text: Dick: That's correct and consistent with the round-end steps in Wingspan (see the Oceania rulebook or the round-end tile in Oceania; Asia too). Round-end powers are first, then any unused nectar is discarded.

127032.author: Íris
127032.text: Can there be a translation of the Expansap Oceania rules into Portuguese?

127033.author: Jamey Stegmaier
127033.text: We would love for Divercentro to make that-please let them know you want it! :)

127122.author: John Ritchie
127122.text: Yellow-Headed Blackbird. It's Brown Power says 'Tuck 1 bird card from your hand behind this bird. If you do, you may also lay 1 egg on this bird.' If I have already laid its egg limit (3) can I still tuck 1 bird card, even though I won't be able to lay any more eggs?

127125.author: Jamey Stegmaier
127125.text: You can still tuck the bird, but since you're at egg capacity, you can't lay an egg.

127301.author: Al
127301.text:
This question regards automa rules for Oceania powers. It says:

When you need to 'check if another player has something in their supply', if automa has any cubes on this round's goal tile, she has the necessary item...

I'm confused about there being cubes on this round's tile, but the tiles aren't scored until the end of the round. Could you please clarify this rule?

Thank you!

127316.author: David Studley
127316.text:
Hi Al. You are correct that the tiles aren't scored until the end. But, the Automa will place or remove a cube (or do nothing) during each of her turns. We use the number of cubes there to resolve some of the interactive bird powers, such as "If the player to your right has a rodent in their supply..." In this case, the number of cubes on the tile, represent the number of rodents the Automa has in their supply.

Hope that helps. Have fun.

David

127928.author: Hunt
127928.text:
Hey there,

Back with another weird question.

I noticed on the back of the European box that Citizen Scientist (which counts birds with tucked cards) is misrepresented as 10% of cards, when the actual card says 21%. I could not figure out why there is a discrepancy. My Europe box says it's from 2019. Has this been fixed yet? It hasn't changed on the website.

127933.author: Jamey Stegmaier
127933.text: Good eye! The actual printed card is correct.

127986.author: Candace Kern
127986.text:
Hello, this question might have been asked in the past, but we would be grateful for clarification:

Text of Wingspan Bonus Card:

BIRD FEEDER

Birds that eat seeds.

5 to 7 Birds: 3

8+ Birds: 7

Any bird with seed symbol. The bird may also eat other kinds of food.

44% of cards.

No Expansion Symbol on card; a Base Game Bonus Card?

QUESTION: Does the Wild Food Symbol count toward the bonus as a seed?

127995.author: Jamey Stegmaier
127995.text: Thanks for asking! The wild symbol does not count.

128469.author: Michelle Styles
128469.text: The Crimson Chat says "Discard a food from your supply to tuck 1 card from the deck behind this bird".  Can a player discard a nectar?  If so, does it go into the spent pile on the player board?

128471.author: Michelle Styles
128471.text: The House Crow says "Cache 1 food from your supply on each bird in this row".  Can a player cache a nectar?  If so, does it go on the bird or in the spent pile on the player board?

128474.author: Michelle Styles
128474.text: Thank you for such a quick response! We absolutely love this game!

128628.author: Rob M.
128628.text: Hi, could you please consider adding extinct birds sometime in the future? It would be great to see the dodo, Carolina parakeet, passenger pigeon, and moa in the game. Thanks.

128629.author: Rob M.
128629.text:
I’m not familiar with the fan art box. Would the folding box fit inside the base game box? If so, I’d use it for storage rather than recycling it, if it’s sturdy enough.

Which box I’d prefer depends on the mechanism that the expansion is adding. The only expansion I’ve kept separate is Asia for the two-player module. If the new expansion is for specific player counts or significantly changes the game, I’d probably keep it separate and would prefer a two-piece box. If it’s like Oceania, which was more of a general upgrade/update, I’d add it to the base game box and keep the expansion box for part of the storage system.

128630.author: Jamey Stegmaier
128630.text: Definitely, it’s our most request promo pack! :)

128631.author: Jamey Stegmaier
128631.text: The box isn't designed to fit inside of another box, but it is sturdy. Most likely the box with include a card tray, which is designed to go in an existing box.

129537.author: Joshua Elshof
129537.text:
The Galah card says: choose 1 other player. They reset the bird feeder and gain a wheat, if there is one. You tuck 2 cards from the deck behind this bird.

Can you tuck two cards regardless of if they gain a wheat or is them gaining a wheat a requirement to tuck the two cards?

129538.author: Jamey Stegmaier
129538.text: Great question! You can tuck 2 cards regardless of if they gain a wheat.

129994.author: Parmida
129994.text:
Hello,

For the bird cards that indicate "choose any 1 die and roll ..." or " choose any 3 dice and roll..." do we return the rerolled dice to the birdfeeder or we keep it outside until the birdfeeder is reset?

129995.author: Jamey Stegmaier
129995.text: You'll roll them outside of the birdfeeder. Thanks for playing!

130736.author: Marina Simionescu
130736.text:
I have a question about the end-game scoring in Duet mode, specifically the part where players score points for the largest contiguous group of their Duet tokens on the shared Duet board.

If I have my tokens placed in a shape, like this (all Xs are mine):

      X - X

                 \

                   X - X

                /

            X

         /      \

X - X ---  X - X

Does this count as a contiguous group of 9 tokens or only 7?

130737.author: Jamey Stegmaier
130737.text: Marina, I want to answer accurately, and I appreciate the effort to convey this in text. I'm worried that I may not have a perfect answer for you based on this diagram, so could you instead take a photo of the board state and post it to the Wingspan Facebook group with this question?

130738.author: Marina Simionescu
130738.text: To better illustrate what I mean, here’s an image of the token placement I’m referring to:  https://imgur.com/a/llcQa44

130740.author: Jamey Stegmaier
130740.text: That's perfect! It's a contiguous group of 9 tokens. :)

130741.author: Marina Simionescu
130741.text: Thank you so much for the quick reply – you just ended a two-day argument! :) Much appreciated!

131499.author: Emma
131499.text: Are the digital versions of the game cross-platform? I have a friend who plays on steam, but I'd love to play on my switch. Could we still play together? Or would I also need to get a steam account to play with her? Thanks! :)

131500.author: Jamey Stegmaier
131500.text: I'm sorry, Emma, but my understanding is that the way Monster Couch set up the game, it can't be played cross-platform.

131668.author: Andrew Richardson
131668.text: Hey this is an awesome game! My wife and I have been playing nonstop for a couple weeks now. Given the main game has 170 bird cards plus the many expansions is there any tips or tricks to properly shuffling all the cards without damaging them. They’re nice cards and we don’t want to bend them. Thanks for the advice!!

131687.author: Jamey Stegmaier
131687.text: Thanks for playing! I typically just divide them into a few stacks and shuffle each one a few times, mixing them as I go.

132643.author: Jeremy Payne
132643.text: When drawing a card, either bonus or bird, do you have to draw from the top of the deck? Or can you draw from anywhere in that deck?

133137.author: Stephen C Van Nostrand
133137.text:
How is play order determined within end-of-games powers? As far as I can tell, it's only relevant for the specific combination of Kākāpō and another player with either Indian Vulture or Greater Adjutant.

Kākāpō (Oceania): Game End: Draw 4 bonus cards, keep 1, and discard the other 3.

Indian Vulture (Asia): Game End: Copy one bonus card of the player on your right, as if it were your own (score it based on your own birds).

Greater Adjutant (Asia): Game End: Copy one bonus card of the player on your left, as if it were your own (score it based on your own birds).

133140.author: Jamey Stegmaier
133140.text: In the rare cases when it matters, activate them in clockwise order starting with the player who has the first-player token.

133143.author: Catie R
133143.text: Are there plans to improve the “couch co-op” functionality of the game on the Switch? We’d love to be able to play online, together, with friends, without having to either play as a team or keep signing in and out of our individual Nintendo accounts. Thank you! Love the game, love the online ability to play with friends who are not close by.

133144.author: Jamey Stegmaier
133144.text: Feel free to ask Monster Couch about that—we (Stonemaier Games) only handle the tabletop versions of our games.

133490.author: Nancy
133490.text:
Question:

I see that some of the cards in the Asia addition are repeats. Can you tell me which ones?

133491.author: Jamey Stegmaier
133491.text: There are no repeats in Asia or any expansion. Each bird is unique.

133530.author: Nancy
133530.text: I mean that some of them are in the original game, so there are doubles if you put them all together!

133531.author: Jamey Stegmaier
133531.text: There are no duplicates within or across the expansion. In other words, no card in Wingspan Asia is also found in the core game of Wingspan or any other expansion. If you have a specific card in mind, there is the slim possibility that we missed one (feel free to mention the card by name so I can look it up), but I'm not aware of any duplicates at all.

133541.author: Michael
133541.text:
Hi,

Is there any plan about releasing a Nordic version of this Asia expansion like the other expansions?

133542.author: Jamey Stegmaier
133542.text: We only make English-language products, but you're welcome to ask Asmodee Nordics!

134235.author: Cass
134235.text:
Can you refuse to gain a bird card or bonus card after you've already looked at it or looked at a set of cards you get to choose from? I know the general rule is that benefits are always optional, but does that apply even after time you've drawn the card? 

This came up in a two-player digital game. My opponent had Greater Adjutant that let's then copy one of my bonus cards. I had played Philippine Eagle and rolled three rats right off the bat so I chose to draw two bonus cards. But both bonus cards would have resulted in my opponent getting more net points than me and I was surprised that the digital implementation let me choose to draw no card after seeing them. Is this correct?

And if it is correct, what about the Black-tailed Godwit whose power is "Draw 1 new bonus card. Then draw 3 card and keep 1 of them." Could you draw a bonus card and choose not to keep it but then still draw 3 bird cards?

134251.author: Jamey Stegmaier
134251.text: If you choose to activate a power, you must follow through with it to completion.

134869.author: Jessi
134869.text: There are duplicate bonus cards. They are not exactly the same so not technically duplicate but maybe that is what they are referring to.

134870.author: Jamey Stegmaier

David

137413.author: Levi
137413.text: This is a basic rules question that I'm sure has been answered ad nauseum but posting for my sanity. If a player is gaining two or more food and the bird feeder only has, say, two dice in it, can that player gain one of those food, then re-roll the bird feeder before gaining the rest of their food? This is definitely the case in the digital versions, but there has been some question as to its validity in the tabletop version. I have to admit, the language in the rules could definitely be more explicit—it almost sounds like you can only re-roll (if available) either before you take any food or that you must gain whatever's in the bird feeder, then re-roll if you empty it and still need to gain more food for that turn. Thanks in advance!

137414.author: Jamey Stegmaier
137414.text: Absolutely yes! You gain food one at a time for that purpose.

140638.text:
Laughing Gull Pink Power: "When another player resets the birdfeeder, gain 1 die from the birdfeeder at the end of their turn.

Who exactly caused the birdfeeder to be reset isn't always clear.  Let's assume Player A has Laughing Gull and the the Australian Owlet-Nightjar ("When another player takes the "gain food" action, gain 1 invertebrate from the birdfeeder, if there is one, at the end of their turn.").

On Player B's turn gaining food, there is 1 grub in the feeder.  Due to the Nightjar, Player A gains 1 grub.  Player B rolls the feeder, since being empty triggers a re-roll.  

Should Player A then gain a food via the Laughing Gull or not? i.e. who rerolled the feeder?  Is it simply enough that the feeder was rolled on Player B's turn?

140646.text: It's simply enough that the feeder was reset on Player B's turn.

142592.author: Henry C Iverson
142592.text: What was the reasoning behind having just one expansion cover South America, Central America, and the Caribbean, when all three areas have so much bird diversity?

142593.author: Jamey Stegmaier
142593.text:
Our plan has always been 1 expansion per continent, not multiple expansions for each continent.

The real question is why is Central America in an expansion that could have just been South America, especially since the core game was for all of North America? The truth is that the core game primarily covers the birds of the US and some in Canada, so we wanted to better represent the entire area south of the US. Hence why this expansion has by far more birds than any previous expansion (111 birds + 40 hummingbirds).

"How does the smaller Hummingbird cards affect the Hummingbird cards already in the game?"

The original hummingbirds work exactly as they’ve always worked. They fit into Wingspan’s balance in their original form, just as the small hummingbird cards are balanced in their deck of 40.

"The Hummingbird column board, instead of overlaying it on the last column on the playmat. Can you add it to the end?"

It is not designed for that.

"Can you play the new smaller Humingbird card, Hummingbird Column boards and the garden as a separate mini-game?"

"Will you create a narrate campaign expansion to allow Wingspan player to enjoy the total Wingspan experience by playing their collection through each continent and maybe biome?"

The Rufous Hornero reads, "When Played: Place 1 egg on the first empty slot in each habitat. When you play a bird on each slot, discard the egg there and count it towards the bird's egg cost."

You can only use the egg for the bird played on top of the egg. And if you don't need the egg to play the bird (column 1), discard the egg.

149440.author: Jamey Stegmaier

150267.author: Martha
150267.text: When playing the Rufous Hornero, eggs get placed on the first empty slots in each habitat. If the eggs remain on empty slots (no cards played in those slots), do the eggs count towards end-of-round goals (ie. eggs in the grasslands) and the end-of-game egg tally?

"These eggs are placeholders; they do not count as eggs in your preserve for any other purpose. The spaces are still empty for purposes of bird powers that count empty spaces."

Based on that, the eggs do not count towards any goals.

153318.author: Berend-Jan
153318.text:
"Tui" in combination with "Lineated woodpecker"

I have "Tui" in my forest as rightmost bird and my neighbour has the "Lineated woodpecker"in the forest as rightmost bird.

Tui says:

WHEN ACTIVATED: Copy a brown power on one bird in the forest of the player to your left.

"Lineated woodpecker"in the forest as most rightbird.

WHEN ACTIVATED: If this is the rightmost bird in its habitat, move it with the action cube to another habitat and continue your turn in the new habitat.

So I activate "Tui" and want to copy the brown power of the "Lineated woodpecker".

Two questions:

Does that mean I can move my "Tui" out of the forest to another habitat, although normally "Tui" is a "forest only" bird? 

And do both "Tui" and the "Lineated woodpecker" recquire to be rightmost bird?

153323.author: Travis Willse
153323.text:
When a bird copies another bird's power, it behaves as if it has that power (until the end of the turn, in the case of a brown or white power), after which the copied bird plays no further role. So, if the Tūī copies the Lineated Woodpecker's power:

(1) The Tūī may indeed move to another habitat: The habitat icon on the Tūī restricts where it can be played, not where it can be moved.

(2) After copying, the power only checks whether the bird currently being activated (the Tūī), so as long as the Tūī is the rightmost bird in its habitat, it can use the rest of its power, regardless of whether the Lineated Woodpeck is the rightmost bird in its habitat.

The same comments apply to the Tūī copying the simpler "migration" power from the core game (e.g., Common Nighthawk, "WHEN ACTIVATED: If this bird is to the right of all other birds in its habitat, move it to another habitat."). For more discussion and the official ruling, please see this post in the official FB group: https://www.facebook.com/groups/wingspanboardgame/permalink/677258919644380/?comment_id=677284199641852&reply_comment_id=677287326308206).

157465.author: Jamey Stegmaier

3. The tracks are meant to be equal in power.

158954.author: Joe Aubrey
158954.text:
Hi Dylan! Here are the answers to your questions...

Wester Capercaillie: You can't skip giving one bonus card to another player (you can't skip costs). You could gain only 1 and give it away, but I'm not sure why you'd choose that.

Canada Jay: "Cache 1 wild from your personal supply on this bird and/or gain 1 food of a type cached on this bird from the general supply."

Yes, you can cache 1 and then immediately gain that type of food from the general supply.

Pink powers, "When another player resets the birdfeeder": Yes, when the birdfeeder is reset due to player actions (like when it become empty after a player takes the last food), this pink power triggers.

How much will this game cost?

Stonemaier serves multiple regions (4 different Shopify storefronts), with minor price variations based on exchange rates and how sales tax is applied in each region. (I see that you are pretty open on the blogs and newsletters about the various parts of the business, which is sort of how I have the audacity to inquire about this...)

161680.author: Jamey Stegmaier
161680.text:
We let each localization partner pick what's best for them for bonus cards like that; some choose to use the English names or to adjust the bonus card points; others have some alternative bonus cards. Here's a general article about how we work with localization partners: https://stonemaiergames.com/working-with-localization-partners-in-2026/

The promo pack pricing is based on the price of the Wingspan European Expansion, which is basically a cards-only expansion. It has 81 bird cards and an MSRP of $30, so that's around $0.37 per card, which results in a price of $9-$10 per bird promo pack (or $7-$8 if you're a Stonemaier Champion). The initial intention wasn't for people to buy all 6 packs, at least not all at once.

165076.author: Patricia Christensen
165076.text:
I can’t remember what the birds name was but it was a brown power which said that I had to reset the bird feeder and then take all the seeds and cash the rodent. Now to my question in two scenarios:

If I reset the bird feeder and there are 3 dice with seeds and then 2 dice with fish - can I reset the bird feeder again to see if there are any rodents? Or is my turn finished when I take the seeds? 

Does it make a difference if all the dice are with seeds and then the bird feeder is empty, then it’ll automatically be reset - but when I do that, can I then cash the rodent or will my turn end after resetting? 

If your answer in one or both of these scenarios is that I’m allowed to reset and take rodents, what about the seeds if there are any after resetting?

165088.author: Jamey Stegmaier
165088.text:
Thanks for your question, Patricia. I would have to see that specific power, but the general rule is that whenever you're gaining food (even in the middle of gaining food), if all dice in the birdfeeder are exactly the same, you can reset it. It seems to me that both of these situations would let you gain the seeds, reset, then cache the rodent.

"If your answer in one or both of these scenarios is that I’m allowed to reset and take rodents, what about the seeds if there are any after resetting?" I think this depends on the exact wording of the power. If you find it, please let me know. Using Wingsearch (linked near the top of this page) might help.

165105.author: Patricia Christensen
165105.text: Thank you for your reply. It is the Red-legged Seriema.

165106.author: Jamey Stegmaier
165106.text: Thanks! The way I read this particular card is that you're looking at the birdfeeder status after a single reset (simultaneously looking for grain and rodents). So for this card, I would not say that you could claim some of those tokens and then reset again to gain more.

165152.author: Philip

165155.author: Jamey Stegmaier
165155.text: The Motmot says that all players draw a bird blind from a food deck. That means you'll draw the top card of a food deck and flip it over to become a bird. It's one of the very few times in Wingspan Pocket when the card you draw doesn't stay on the same side as it is drawn.

168529.author: David Studley

Have fun!

168588.author: Jamey Stegmaier
168588.text: Thanks for playing! The active player chooses first, then players go clockwise. And yes, as long as the matching food icon is on the card, it is eligible.

168594.author: Alexia Hill

168697.author: Brendan Dunne
168697.text:
Hey team, I have another question for a new bird in the Americas expansion. 

The Muscovy Duck has a round-end power that says "attract up to two hummingbirds." Does this power check if there are two hummingbird slots open right when it's activated, or can I attract one hummingbird, get another of the hummingbird slots open, and then attract another?

I had a game recently where I had this duck in play, but only one hummingbird slot open at the end of the round. There was a way I could attract one hummingbird to open up another slot, but I wasn't sure if the duck needs two hummingbird slots to be free at the time the power is activated in order for you to attract to, or if it checks one at a time.

Hope this comment makes sense. Also, just as an aside, the long long comments threads across a couple diff pages on your site have always been the Bible when I'm checking rulings on cards, but the new way they display where you have to go page by page makes it way harder to search one card/term and see the full history of rules questions. Would love if there's some way to make all these questions and answers visible on a single page somewhere—otherwise finding old rulings calls gets quite difficult.

Thank you always.

168698.author: Jamey Stegmaier
168698.text:
Technically, none of the above (and you're on the page for Wingspan, which has different rules than Wingspan Pocket, questions for which can be posted here: https://stonemaiergames.com/games/wingspan/wingspan-pocket/).

The optional rule on page 6 is: "At any time while drawing cards, if 3 or more food cards in the Supply are exactly the same, you may discard all matching cards at once."

This can happen whenever you're drawing/gaining cards.

30838.author: Jamey Stegmaier

31323.author: John Neeve

31329.author: Jamey Stegmaier

31473.author: Joshua J Hill
31473.text: Regarding the birds that have the "when played you may play a second bird from your hand, pay its costs as normal" ability, when it says a second bird is that an implied limit on the number of birds i am able to chain with these cards? For example if I have 3 birds in hand and 2 of them have the above-mentioned ability, as long as I can pay the costs involved with playing them, am I able to play out my hand that turn?

31474.author: Jamey Stegmaier
31474.text: Joshua: Definitely, as long as you can play the food and egg costs, you can keep chaining them.

31498.author: John Neeve
31498.text:
30 Automa games and I’ve encountered something new.

The American Oystercatcher says ‘When played: draw cards equal to the number of players +1. Take 1, pass them on, each player selects one and passes them on. You keep the extra one.

When playing against the Automa I have a few options.

1.  Draw 3, Choose one, give Automa A  bird that fits his criteria (or face down if it doesn’t fit) from the remaining two and keep the last one. (This what I did)

2. Draw 3, Choose two myself and give Automa the last card face up or facedown dependant on fitting his criteria.

3. Draw 3, Choose two and give the Automa nothing.

31499.author: Jamey Stegmaier
31499.text: Thanks John! I've forwarded this to David, but just to let you know, by far the best places to post questions about Wingspan are on BGG or the Wingspan Facebook group. You're welcome to post here, but I just wanted to let you know that your great questions will help more people if they're posted in one of those other locations. :)

31504.author: Jamey Stegmaier
31504.text: David says, "The answer is 3. You draw 3, keep 2. The Automa gets nothing, as usual."

31508.author: David Studley
31508.text: Thanks, Jamey.  This was an edge case and we had a good discussion about it on BGG, if you're interested. https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2126943/automa-american-oystercatcher  Following the spirit of the American Oystercatcher, not only do you gain 2 cards, but you get the added benefit of choosing from 3.

31554.author: Patrick
31554.text:
Hi. Just a question about a card that says 'when activated'  you take a certain piece of food from the feeder (when available) and you MAY keep it on the card. 31555.author: Jamey Stegmaier
31555.text: If it says that you "may" place the food on the card, you have the option of either keeping the food in your supply (to later spend) or to cache it on the bird card (for 1 VP at the end of the game).

32147.author: Jamey Stegmaier
32147.text: That's referring to a predatory's ability triggering for a positive result. Like, if a bird goes hunting for another bird and it fails (maybe the wingspan of the revealed bird is too big), that's a failure.

Hey Jaime!

If The Mockingbird is the right most bird in the habitat, can it “repeat” a birds power to the left, even though it hasn’t happened yet? Thanks and LOVE all your games!!

33450.author: Jamey Stegmaier
33450.text:
It copies another power in that habitat (on a bird to the left or right of it).

EDIT: This has been revised. The Mockingbird and other birds like it, cause another bird to activate in the same row. It does not "copy" the power itself.

33540.author: ZED

WHEN ACTIVATED: Each player gains

1 food from the birdfeeder, starting

with the player of your choice.

33541.author: Jamey Stegmaier
33541.text: You are a player, so you can certainly chose yourself. If you were required to choose another player, the card would say, "starting with another player."

33576.author: Jamey Stegmaier
33576.text: It's egg limit is 0. It cannot hold eggs.

33594.author: Miguel Albornoz
33594.text: When you have the yellow breasted chat and you move it to another habitat, do you continue playing your action piece to the left in the new habitat or the old one? (E.g. I play draw a card, get to the chat, and move it to the forest. Do I continue to move to the left in the forest or the wetland?

33598.author: Jamey Stegmaier
33598.text: Your action tokens remains in the original habitat, as that's the action you selected to take that turn.

33720.author: Merri
33720.text: Two questions from our maiden game yesterday: 1) once you choose to activate a bird's powers, is it a one-time thing? Or if you place another bird to the right on a subsequent turn, can you use the same activation powers again? 2) once you have 15 birds on your board during the 4-part round, what happens if you have other bird cards along with the food and egg costs, but nowhere to put them? Thanks.

33721.author: Jamey Stegmaier
33721.text:
1. Every time you activate a habitat, you have the choice of activating each "when activated" ability from right to left.

2. If you're able to fill up your board with birds (which can happen, though it's very rare-if it's happening to you a lot, it's possible you may be playing a rule incorrectly), you cannot play more birds.

33722.author: Merri
33722.text: Thanks! By "activating a habitat" do you mean placing a bird card in one of the five spaces?

33723.author: Jamey Stegmaier
33723.text: I'm referring to the 3 actions that are not "play a bird". For example, if you use your turn to gain food, you gain some food from the birdfeeder and then activate "when activated" birds from right to left in the forest habitat.

33777.author: Sebastian
33777.text:
Question from our maiden game: several actions include a “draw a [image of rear face of bird card]“ instruction. Does this include the bird cards that are placed face up on the card holder or only the stack of face down bird cards? When can the face up bird cards be drawn, only when playing the “draw a bird card” action?

Is it correct that at the end of a round the bird feeder is not restocked with all dice / the dice are not re-rolled?

33779.author: Jamey Stegmaier
33779.text:
Whenever you draw a bird card, unless otherwise specified, it's from either the deck or the 3 face-up birds.

That is correct about the birdfeeder.

34224.author: Seb
34224.text:
When taking the “draw bird cards” action, players may have the option to discard an egg for an additional bird card. Does a player need to decide at the beginning of his/her turn whether he/she wants to exercise that option (before having drawn any bird cards) or may he/she look at the drawn bird card(s) and then decide whether to exercise the option?

(Similarly, when taking the “gain food from bird feeder action” and deciding whether to exercise the option of discarding a bird card for an additional food die.)

34226.author: Jamey Stegmaier
34226.text: A player may look at the cards they've drawn (you can select from the face-up cards or the top of the deck) and then decide whether or not to exercise the option. Same with gaining food.

3 sets (because there are 3 eggs per row)

2 sets (because you've 2 sets in the first column, and none in the 3rd column)

1 set (because you only count each bird once it has an egg on it).

34373.author: Jamey Stegmaier

34490.author: Jordan Herron

34497.author: Yves Roels

34501.author: Jamey Stegmaier

34503.author: Jamey Stegmaier
34503.text: Oh okay, I read this incorrectly. You are indeed looking at eggs in the rows. If you have 3 eggs in each row, that's what matters.

34663.author: Mark
34663.text: It means for example if someone else activates the hunter power that says "Look at a bird from the deck. If wingspan <75cm, tuck behind this bird" and it is in fact <75cm then you can activate that pink power. Similarly for the other hunter (like if they roll a rat/fish to cache one on their card, that means they succeeded and you can activate the power). Keep in mind that you can only activate the pink power between turns. So if multiple people's hunters succeed between your previous turn and the next, you can only activate it once.

34668.author: Stan
34668.text: If the last player in a round (e.g., Round 2) plays the Draw Bird Cards option and selects one (or more) of the three face up cards, do you replace the chosen card(s) from the deck before the remaining face-up cards are removed (and replaced) for the start of the next round?

34669.author: Jamey Stegmaier
34669.text: Technically yes, but because those cards are going to be immediately discarded, I'd recommend not doing so. It's random either way.

34670.author: Stan
34670.text: One advantage (?) of displaying the replacement card(s) before immediately discarding it / them at the end of the round is knowing which bird(s) will no longer be available to help achieve bonus card goals or end-of-round goals.

34870.author: Abby Stewart
34870.text:

34871.author: Jamey Stegmaier
34871.text: Right, you only deal once. But you can gain new cards throughout the game by using the wetland action.

34885.author: Abby
34885.text:
When you take an action (eg gain food or lay eggs), and there are already birds placed in that habitat, how many foods, eggs, cards do you get? (a) the number in the original left most column; (b) the number under the last bird placed; or (c) the number showing in the rightmost place.

Thank you!

34886.author: Jamey Stegmaier
34886.text: Abby: The number showing in the space to the right of the last bird in that habitat. So, if you have 2 birds in the habitat, the benefits you gain at the beginning of that action are in the middle column (the 3rd slot).

34887.author: Abby

34960.author: Gloria

 please, If a bird -when activated (and on the right) can move to another habitat- does the moved bird gain anything from the new position -as food, eggs, cards? Or is it just a shift in position? Thank you.

34961.author: Jamey Stegmaier

34962.author: Gloria hubacker
